title: A gift across the sea
label: FRIENDSHIP
text: In autumn 2019, Japan gifted 125 cherry trees to the Royal Parks as part of the Japan–UK Season of Culture. Their spring flowers make that cultural exchange part of London's living landscape.

title: A welcome for spring
label: A SHARED TRADITION
text: The same cultural season brought 6,500 new cherry trees to sites across the UK. In Japan, hanami brings people together beneath the blossoms; the Royal Parks note that this flower-viewing tradition has also become popular in some London parks.

title: The Great White Cherry
label: A REMARKABLE RETURN
text: English horticulturist Collingwood ‘Cherry’ Ingram helped restore the Great White Cherry, or Taihaku, in Japan. After seeing a painting of the tree there in 1926, he used cuttings from a Sussex garden to help bring the variety back.

title: Here for a moment
label: THE BLOOM
text: Cherry blossom can shift from deep pink through pale pink to white, and some varieties begin greenish-yellow. The display usually lasts only a week or two, with wind and rain able to shorten it.
